verdict.rationale: Ramp exposes a broad programmable surface: an OpenAPI spec with 174 paths, granular OAuth read/write scopes covering bills, cards, funds, reimbursements, approvals, travel, treasury and more, plus a JSON-mode CLI and an OAuth-gated MCP server that cover most UI workflows (approvals, edits, card locks, purchases). However, Ramp never claims UI parity, and the docs show tasks that still require the UI: developer app creation happens in the dashboard, MCP access restrictions are set in the dashboard, and bill approvals 'aren't yet available via MCP — use the Ramp UI or the Blank Canvas Approvals API'. Missing for 10: an explicit API/UI parity statement, API-based admin setup (app creation, MCP access configuration), confirmed coverage of UI-only features such as travel auto-rebooking and policy/workflow configuration, and independent hands-on corroboration.
